title: Comelec logs over 170,000 voter registrations for 2028 elections

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Commission on Elections (Comelec) has received more than 107,000 voter applications in a week since it resumed its registration drive for the 2028 elections.

According to data provided by Comelec Chairperson George Erwin Garcia to reporters on Thursday, the poll body processed 107,346 voter registrations. Comelec reopened registration on November 10, and the drive will run until July 30, 2027.
The Comelec also noted that female voter registrants (58,762) outnumbered male registrants (49,076).

Meanwhile, Calabarzon (Cavite, Laguna, Batangas, Rizal, and Quezon) logged the highest number of applications, with 26,934, followed by the National Capital Region with 20,151 and Central Luzon with 11,662.

The poll body earlier said it was optimistic that it would exceed its target of registering three million additional voters for the much-anticipated 2028 elections. It also noted long queues at registration sites across the country when it resumed the drive.
Many of those who lined up on the first day of the resumed voter registration were young Filipinos. Garcia earlier said that seeing the youth register to vote was a “good indication.”
Interested voter registrants can submit their applications through the local offices of their respective election officers, satellite or mall registration sites, and the Register Anywhere Program.
Aside from first-time registration, the poll body said it can also accommodate requests for transfer and reactivation of registration, as well as modifications to details in existing records.
To register as a voter, an individual must be at least 18 years old on or before election day on May 8, 2028.
They must also have resided in the Philippines for at least one year and in the place where they intend to vote for at least six months immediately preceding the elections.
An applicant must present any of the following valid IDs, along with a photocopy:

items: Student ID or library card signed by a school authority
Social Security System or Government Service Insurance System ID, or other Unified Multi-Purpose ID
Integrated Bar of the Philippines ID card
Certificate of Confirmation issued by the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples, for members of Indigenous Cultural Communities or Indigenous Peoples
Other valid government-issued IDs that meet Comelec’s requirements
